No CHURN_FILES passed (state.json hotspot_history is stale, dated 2026-05, pointing at api-server routes that map to already-reviewed segments). Selection fell to oldest-unreviewed from state.review_cursor: mobile-native-kmp (2026-08-25) is the true oldest but is EXCLUDED per assignment (cloud-unlandable — AGP egress-403). Next oldest is reality-server (2026-08-28); every other landable segment sits at 2026-08-29. Saturation check passed: zero OPEN code-review-finding rows in backlog.json for any segment (18 total, all done). Primary expert = Rust, no secondary (per segment->expert map). Static-only: grep sweep of backend/servers/reality-server/src (43 .rs) for unwrap/expect/unsafe/todo/panic/dynamic-SQL/PII-in-logs/limit-clamping/owner-scoping, then targeted reads of security-critical hot spots (sso.rs cookie flags, extractors/auth.rs, agency_branding.rs authz, reports.rs anonymous path, agent_reviews.rs input validation, the three background alert drainers). Sibling Tier-1d runs today already emitted the byte-vs-char length bug, the report-contact gap, the SSO negcache-poison + per-call-client findings, and the drainer i18n gap; this run avoided those and surfaced one remaining distinct defect.
note: reality-server is a mature, multiply-audited codebase and the high-severity classes are CLEAN under this pass: all non-test unwrap/expect are startup-config fail-fast (state.rs JWT_SECRET panics), OS-rng failures (acceptable), or guarded (extractors/auth.rs:63 strip_prefix is gated by the same closure's starts_with predicate; handlers/inquiries/mod.rs:274 chars().next().unwrap() is gated by the is_empty() early-return at :269, and the subsequent cleaned[1..] byte-slice is safe because reaching it proves the first char is ASCII '+' or an ASCII digit = 1 byte). No unsafe. SSO session cookies are always HttpOnly+Secure+SameSite=Strict scoped to /api/v1/sso (build_portal_session_cookie, sso.rs:1368-1380). Every list endpoint clamps limit/offset (listings clamp_pagination #953 regression-tested; portal_listings, saved_searches, reports, agent_reviews, articles, realtors all clamp; agency_imports uses a fixed LIMIT 100). No secrets in tracing calls; no format!-interpolated SQL in this segment (dynamic sort delegated to the db repo; in-segment ORDER BY is all static). All user-scoped mutations pass principal.user_id / an is_active membership check (no IDOR). The background alert drainers (search_alert_drainer, favorite_alerts, saved_search_alerts) handle every DB/transport error per-item with no panic path that could kill the spawned loop. The single finding below is the one distinct, landable defect that survived: an input-validation asymmetry in the agency-branding update handler, confined to one reality-server route file with a clean self-contained fix.

evidence: update_branding (routes/agency_branding.rs:244, PUT /api/v1/agencies/{id}/branding) validates the three URL fields of UpdateBrandingRequest with check_optional_url_field (agency_branding.rs:252-254) — the code comment at :250-251 states this is the 'H7' guard, added precisely because logo_url/banner_url/watermark_url 'end up in on the frontend' and must reject javascript:/data:/file: schemes. But the two free-text fields in the SAME struct, primary_color and secondary_color (UpdateBrandingRequest, agency_branding.rs:130-131, typed Option), receive NO validation of any kind before being bound raw into the INSERT ... ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE at agency_branding.rs:321-329 (bound at :324-325).

These color values are read back by the UNAUTHENTICATED public getter get_branding (GET /api/v1/agencies/{id}/branding, agency_branding.rs:155-) and, per the branding feature's purpose, rendered into the reality-web agency page's styling (inline style / CSS custom properties). An arbitrary string in a color slot is therefore both a data-integrity hazard (garbage like 'notacolor' silently breaks the agency's public page for every visitor) and a stored CSS-injection / potential XSS surface if the frontend interpolates the value into a style context without its own sanitization — the exact class of DOM-reaching-input risk the author already recognized and defended for the sibling URL fields, left unguarded here.

Severity is LOW (+1): the write is gated behind an is_active agency-membership check (agency_branding.rs:277-296), so this is not an anonymous-write injection — exploitation requires a malicious or compromised agency member, and the ultimate XSS depends on frontend rendering not verified in this static pass. But the read side is fully public, so a single bad member value degrades the page for all visitors, and the asymmetry with the H7-validated URL fields makes this a clear consistency/defense-in-depth gap.

Fix: mirror the URL-field guard with a small color validator — accept only a strict pattern (e.g. ^#[0-9A-Fa-f]{3,8}$ for hex, or an explicit allowlist of rgb()/hsl()/named-color forms) for primary_color and secondary_color before the INSERT, returning 400 with a generic message (do NOT echo the offending value back — same reflected-XSS caution the file already documents for attachment URLs). Self-contained change in agency_branding.rs; IG3 via a unit/integration test that a non-color primary_color yields 400 while a valid #RRGGBB is accepted.

Confidence medium: the absence of any validation on primary_color/secondary_color and the raw bind into the INSERT are confirmed by static read of the handler and the request struct; 'medium' rather than 'high' because the frontend rendering path that would turn the stored value into executable CSS/XSS was not traced in this static-only pass, and the membership gate bounds who can write.
